subject: Data retention exception for FinTechCo — follow-up & next steps
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Ashley Lin <ashley.lin@fintechco.com>, Peter Thompson <peter.thompson@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-18T15:05:00Z
Subject: Quick follow-up & next steps from today's call — retention exception request

Hi Ashley / Peter,

Thanks again for carving out time today — really helpful to understand FinTechCo's transaction flow and your data minimization needs. Per our conversation, you asked for a formal path for a short-term retention exception for logs that may contain low-scope PII (masked account IDs) for fraud analysis.

Next steps I committed to on the call:
- Share a short summary of the options we can support (0-retention, shortened logs, scoped retention window).
- Attach a simple exception request template you can fill out for legal/procurement.
- Loop in our security lead to confirm what evidence (SOC2, logging controls) we can provide.

Attached: data-retention-exception-request.pdf (template).

Proposed interim option (per call):
- Shortened logs: retain token/interaction metadata for 30 days in prod logs, full request payload KV cache cleared after 24 hours, and sensitive fields are redacted before persisted logs are written.

If that sounds aligned, I can draft the legal language and get Rafael to sign off on the tech controls. Would next Wednesday (6/23) for a quick 20-min sync to review and finalize the exception be good?

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

--
Redwood Inference
www.redwood.ai

From: Ashley Lin <ashley.lin@fintechco.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Peter Thompson <peter.thompson@fintechco.com>
Date: 2027-06-18T17:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up & next steps from today's call — retention exception request

Hi Camila,

Thanks — that summary helps. A few clarifications from our side:
- We prefer 0-retention for full request payloads where possible (no storage of raw PII) but can accept a 24-hour buffered window for troubleshooting if you provide a secure deletion proof.
- For logs, 30 days is on the high side for our compliance team. Can you support a scoped retention of 7 days for logging metadata, with a mechanism to request time-limited access for incident investigation?
- We also need confirmation that logs stored for any period are only accessible by Redwood staff with role-based access and that access is logged (audit trail).

If you can capture those commitments in the exception template, we'll circulate to procurement and legal. Wed 6/23 11:00am PT works for a short sync.

Regards,
Ashley Lin
Head of Security & Compliance
FinTechCo
ashley.lin@fintechco.com

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Ashley Lin <ashley.lin@fintechco.com>
Date: 2027-06-18T18:00:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Quick follow-up & next steps from today's call — retention exception request

Team — forwarding FinTechCo's clarifications. Key asks: 0-retention for payloads preferred (24h buffer acceptable with deletion proof), logs retention limited to 7 days, role-based access + audit trail for any retained logs, and a mechanism for time-limited access on request.

Marissa — can you advise on commercial impact (we had modeled 30 days)?
Rafael — can you confirm whether the runtime currently supports 7-day metadata retention + deletion proof and what evidence we can provide (SOC2 pages, access logs export)?

If we can meet these controls, I will draft a short exception with the exact language and send to Ashley/Peter for legal sign-off.

Thanks,
Camila

> On Jun 18, 2027, at 17:12, Ashley Lin <ashley.lin@fintechco.com> wrote:
> > Hi Camila,
> > ...

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Ashley Lin <ashley.lin@fintechco.com>
Date: 2027-06-19T09:14:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Quick follow-up & next steps from today's call — retention exception request

Camila / team / Ashley —

We can support the controls Ashley listed with the following notes (technical & evidence):

1) Payload retention (0-retention preferred):
- We already provide an option to not persist request payloads for hosted API — that can be enabled for FinTechCo at the tenant level.
- For the 24-hour troubleshooting buffer we can implement a strict TTL and provide a deletion confirmation log (signature and timestamp) once the TTL is processed.

2) Logs retention windows:
- We can implement a scoped retention policy to purge log metadata after 7 days. This requires a short ops runbook and a config change; implementation ETA: 5 business days once exception approved.

3) Access controls & audit trail:
- Role-based access is in place (RBAC) and all access to retained logs is recorded. We can provide an export of audit events for a rolling 90 day period filtered for FinTechCo access.

4) Evidence we can provide immediately:
- SOC2-summary.pdf (attached) — covers controls around logging and access.
- Sample deletion confirmation (template) we will use after the TTL job runs.

Suggested legal language snippet for the exception clause you can use in your template: "Redwood agrees to implement a scoped logs retention policy for FinTechCo that retains only metadata for a period of seven (7) days, after which logs are purged. For payloads, Redwood will not persist raw request payloads unless tenant-level 24-hour troubleshooting buffer is explicitly enabled in writing by FinTechCo. Access to retained logs shall be limited to authorized Redwood personnel under RBAC and shall be logged; Redwood will provide audit exports upon request as described in Schedule X."

I'll attach the redwood-logs-retention-sla-draft.docx with the proposed tasks and timeline. If this is acceptable, Camila — feel free to send to FinTechCo.

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Senior Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Ashley Lin <ashley.lin@fintechco.com>, Peter Thompson <peter.thompson@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-20T10:42:00Z
Subject: Retention exception proposal & next steps (doc + e-sign)

Hi Ashley / Peter,

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Per Rafael's note, attached are: (1) a filled exception template with the 7-day logs retention and 24-hour troubleshooting buffer option, (2) the draft SLA/ops tasks for the retention purge job, and (3) our SOC2 summary for your security team.

Attachments: data-retention-exception-request.pdf (completed), redwood-logs-retention-sla-draft.docx, SOC2-summary.pdf

Summary of commitments:
- Logs metadata retention: 7 days, automatic purge thereafter.
- Payloads: default 0-retention; 24-hour buffer optional if tenant-level toggle is enabled in writing by FinTechCo.
- Access: RBAC only; all access logged; audit export provided on request.
- Implementation ETA for the purge job: 5 business days after exception sign-off.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm acceptance of the terms in the attached exception (reply or mark in the DocuSign link below).
2) If accepted, we'll open a short SOW change order and schedule the ops change.
3) Marissa will follow up on pricing if FinTechCo opts into any increased retention or access-intensive workflows.

DocuSign link to sign exception: https://www.docusign.com/prepare/abc123-retention-exception
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/DEAL-3421

Happy to jump on the 6/23 sync at 11am PT to walk through.

Best,
